Project Description  

The project consists of construction of a detached accessory garage at the above referenced property. The property is located within the Residential B Zoning District. The proposed garage is intended to comply with applicable zoning requirements including accessory structure size, setbacks, building coverage, and impervious surface coverage limitations established by the Upper Dublin Township Zoning Ordinance.  

---

2. Proposed Structure  

The detached garage will measure approximately 18 feet in width by 32 feet in depth, resulting in an approximately 576-square-foot building footprint. This footprint is below the 600-square-foot threshold for accessory structures within the Residential B District, permitting use of the minimum four (4) foot side and rear yard setbacks applicable to accessory buildings under the zoning ordinance. The structure will be located outside required front yard setbacks and will function as an accessory structure to the existing single-family residence.  

---

3. Building and Impervious Coverage  

The property contains approximately 23,950 square feet of lot area. The proposed improvements are intended to remain within allowable building coverage and impervious surface coverage limits for the Residential B District.

The existing residence footprint is approximately 2,962 square feet. An existing accessory tool shed will be removed as part of the project.

The proposed garage is intended to maintain compliance with applicable building and impervious surface coverage limitations.

---

4. Foundation and Grading  

The structure will be supported on a reinforced concrete slab-on-grade foundation with footings constructed in accordance with applicable code requirements. The site slopes slightly toward the rear of the proposed garage location, with an estimated 10 to 12 inches of elevation difference across the building footprint, which will be accommodated through grading and slab design.  

---

5. Use  

The detached garage will be used for vehicle storage, household storage, and storage of lawn and maintenance equipment only and will not contain habitable space.  

---

6. Building Design  

The structure will be constructed with 9-foot first floor wall height and a gable roof with an approximate 10:12 pitch. The roof configuration will allow for a second-story loft area accessed via an interior staircase. A window will be provided in the front gable elevation to provide natural light to the loft area.  

The loft area is intended solely for storage and will not include plumbing, heating, or other features associated with habitable space.  

The front elevation will contain primary vehicle access via a 12-foot wide by 8-foot high overhead garage door. The door may be centered on the elevation or slightly offset to accommodate window placement.  

The right elevation will include a 36-inch man door and a minimum 6-foot-wide equipment door to allow access for lawn equipment and similar items. Two to three windows are proposed on this elevation to provide natural lighting.  

The left elevation will include two windows for natural light.  

The rear elevation may incorporate a window depending on final layout.  

---

7. Exterior Materials  

Exterior finishes are anticipated to consist primarily of vinyl siding or comparable durable siding materials, potentially accented with brick elements to complement the architectural character of the existing residence. Roofing materials will consist of architectural shingles to match or complement the dwelling.  

---

8. Electrical Service  

Electrical service will be extended from the existing residence to the garage. A 100-amp subpanel will be installed within the structure to provide power for lighting, receptacles, and operation of the overhead garage door. Exterior wall-mounted lighting fixtures are proposed on the front and right elevations. Space will be reserved within the panel for potential future use.

We are designing a modern, luxury retail clothing store specializing in custom tailoring, formalwear, and premium menswear. The goal is to create a timeless, elegant space that delivers a high-end customer experience while maintaining an efficient workflow for staff.

The architect will be responsible for creating a complete architectural and interior design package, including:

* Floor plan and space planning
* Interior elevations
* Reflected ceiling plan
* Lighting design
* Electrical plan
* Furniture and fixture layout
* Material and finish selections
* Millwork and cabinetry drawings
* Construction details
* 3D renderings of the completed space

Store Requirements

* Luxury storefront with an inviting entrance
* Reception/check-in area
* Comfortable client waiting lounge with premium seating
* Large custom clothing showroom
* Separate wedding and tuxedo display area
* Ready-to-wear suit display section
* Dress shirt, shoe, belt, tie, and accessory displays
* Dedicated fabric gallery with organized fabric books and swatches
* Custom design consultation area
* Measurement and fitting station
* Tailoring/workstation visible to customers while maintaining a clean, luxury appearance
* Three to four spacious fitting rooms with excellent lighting and large mirrors
* Private VIP fitting room
* Storage room for inventory
* Office space
* POS/check-out area
* Coffee and beverage station for clients

Design Style

The design should feel modern, luxurious, warm, and timeless with a boutique atmosphere comparable to premium European tailoring houses.

Preferred design elements include:

* Natural wood finishes
* Stone or marble accents
* Brass or brushed gold details
* Warm neutral color palette
* Premium lighting throughout
* Feature ceiling details
* High-end flooring
* Clean architectural lines
* Large mirrors
* Minimal yet elegant millwork
* Sophisticated display systems
* Comfortable lounge furniture

Lighting

Lighting should highlight clothing, fabrics, and merchandise while creating a warm and welcoming environment. Include:

* Accent lighting
* Display lighting
* Decorative feature lighting
* Pendant fixtures where appropriate
* Cove or indirect ceiling lighting
* Adjustable spotlights for merchandise

Customer Experience

The store should guide customers naturally from the entrance through the showroom, consultation areas, fitting rooms, and checkout while maintaining an open, spacious feel.

The overall experience should communicate craftsmanship, quality, personalization, and luxury from the moment a customer enters the space.

The final design should be practical for daily operations while serving as a premium destination for custom clothing and formalwear.

My husband and I are getting ready to move forward with designing our custom home on our 10-acre property in the Sanger/Fresno County area. We have been working through the layout ourselves in Home Designer Pro and have a pretty clear idea of what we want, but we are looking for an architect/designer who can help refine the floor plan, make sure everything functions well, and ultimately prepare a complete set of plans for permitting and construction.

We are planning a single-story custom home around 3,500 square feet of finished living space, with a large 3-car or larger side-entry garage. We want the house to feel high-end and spacious, but still comfortable and practical for a family with three children. One of our biggest priorities is good flow—we don’t want wasted square footage, excessive hallways, or rooms that feel disconnected from one another.

Overall Style & Feel

We are going for a warm, timeless California/custom-ranch feel rather than something overly modern or trendy. We like open spaces, lots of natural light, higher ceilings, large windows and doors, and strong indoor/outdoor living.

The kitchen, living room, dining area, and backyard/patio are especially important because we entertain frequently. We want the main living areas to feel impressive and spacious while still being functional for everyday family life.

Layout We Are Looking For

We would like:

* 4 bedrooms – primary suite plus three children’s bedrooms
* A private primary suite
* A spacious primary bathroom and walk-in closet
* Separate enclosed toilet room in the primary bathroom
* Large shower and soaking tub
* Long double vanity
* Two of the children’s bedrooms connected through a Jack-and-Jill bathroom
* A separate bathroom arrangement for our daughter’s bedroom
* A bathroom that is easily accessible to guests without having a bathroom door opening directly into the main living room
* A large open kitchen
* Large island with plenty of seating and prep space
* Kitchen sink positioned under a large window overlooking the backyard
* Large refrigerator/freezer area with an integrated or built-in appearance
* Butler’s pantry approximately 7’ x 18’
* Open dining area
* Large living/great room
* Strong connection between the kitchen, living room, dining area and covered back patio
* Mudroom/laundry approximately 14’ x 7’ connecting the garage to the house
* Large 3+ car side-entry garage
* Plenty of storage throughout the house

We would like to keep exterior doors intentional rather than having doors everywhere, while still having a beautiful connection to the backyard.

Kitchen & Entertaining

The kitchen is probably one of the most important spaces for us. We want it to feel grand and high-end, but we also actually cook and entertain, so functionality is extremely important.

We envision a large island, generous walkways, white-oak-style cabinetry, lots of storage, and a large window over the kitchen sink looking toward the backyard. We also want the butler’s pantry to function as an extension of the kitchen rather than feeling like a separate little room.

We want the kitchen, dining and living spaces to accommodate larger gatherings without the house feeling crowded.

Primary Suite

We want the primary suite to feel luxurious without dedicating an unnecessary amount of square footage to it.

For the bathroom, we like a spa-like feel with a large shower, freestanding tub, double vanity, wall-mounted faucets, sconces and an enclosed toilet room. We want the bathroom and closet arrangement to have a natural flow, but we do not want to have to walk through a wet/shower area to access the closet.

Privacy from the main living areas is also important to us.

Children’s Side of the House

We have three children, so their portion of the house needs to work well as they get older.

We would like our boys’ bedrooms to share a Jack-and-Jill bathroom with a shower, and we want our daughter’s bedroom/bathroom arrangement to have good privacy and storage.

Bedroom closets should be accessed from inside the bedrooms rather than through bathrooms whenever possible.

Garage, Laundry & Everyday Function

We would like a large side-entry garage with enough depth and width for larger vehicles, storage and normal everyday use.

The garage should lead into a mudroom/laundry area before entering the main house so there is a functional drop zone for shoes, backpacks, jackets, etc.

We want the “behind-the-scenes” spaces of the house—pantry, laundry, storage and garage—to be just as thoughtfully designed as the main rooms.

Property & Site

The home will be built on our approximately 10-acre property in the Sanger area of Fresno County. We already have a well on the property and have had the property surveyed.

Because we have a larger property, we would also like help making sure the orientation of the house makes sense for the site, including the driveway approach, front elevation, backyard/patio orientation, views, sun exposure and overall placement of the home.

Plans & Services We Need

We are looking for someone who can take our existing ideas/layout and help us turn them into a professional, buildable design.

Ideally, we would like to know whether you provide or coordinate everything necessary for a complete permit/construction plan set, including architectural plans, elevations, roof plan, foundation information, structural engineering, Title 24/energy documentation and any other plans or calculations required by Fresno County.

We are also interested in knowing how much involvement you have during the engineering/permitting process and whether revisions requested by the County are included in your services.

We would like to provide the floor plan we’ve been developing so you can see the direction we are already headed. We are absolutely open to changes—we don’t want someone to simply redraw what we’ve created. We want professional input on flow, proportions, functionality, structural practicality and opportunities to improve the design while keeping the major things that are important to us.

We are also very conscious of construction costs. Our overall goal is to create a beautiful custom home without designing something unnecessarily complicated or expensive to build. We would appreciate an architect who considers construction efficiency while designing.

Could you please let us know:

* What your design process looks like
* What is included in your services
* Whether you provide a complete permit-ready plan set
* What engineering/Title 24 work you handle or coordinate
* Your approximate fee structure for a project of this size
* How revisions are handled
* Your current timeline and availability
* Approximately how long it typically takes to go from initial design to permit-ready plans
* What information you would need from us to provide a proposal

We are excited to finally get this part of the project moving and are looking for someone who will work collaboratively with us to turn what we’ve been planning into a home that functions beautifully for our family.

Thank you,
Haley & Alvaro

My husband and I are getting ready to move forward with designing our custom home on our 10-acre property in the Sanger/Fresno County area. We have been working through the layout ourselves in Home Designer Pro and have a pretty clear idea of what we want, but we are looking for an architect/designer who can help refine the floor plan, make sure everything functions well, and ultimately prepare a complete set of plans for permitting and construction.

We are planning a single-story custom home around 3,500 square feet of finished living space, with a large 3-car or larger side-entry garage. We want the house to feel high-end and spacious, but still comfortable and practical for a family with three children. One of our biggest priorities is good flow—we don’t want wasted square footage, excessive hallways, or rooms that feel disconnected from one another.

Overall Style & Feel

We are going for a warm, timeless California/custom-ranch feel rather than something overly modern or trendy. We like open spaces, lots of natural light, higher ceilings, large windows and doors, and strong indoor/outdoor living.

The kitchen, living room, dining area, and backyard/patio are especially important because we entertain frequently. We want the main living areas to feel impressive and spacious while still being functional for everyday family life.

Layout We Are Looking For

We would like:

* 4 bedrooms – primary suite plus three children’s bedrooms
* A private primary suite
* A spacious primary bathroom and walk-in closet
* Separate enclosed toilet room in the primary bathroom
* Large shower and soaking tub
* Long double vanity
* Two of the children’s bedrooms connected through a Jack-and-Jill bathroom
* A separate bathroom arrangement for our daughter’s bedroom
* A bathroom that is easily accessible to guests without having a bathroom door opening directly into the main living room
* A large open kitchen
* Large island with plenty of seating and prep space
* Kitchen sink positioned under a large window overlooking the backyard
* Large refrigerator/freezer area with an integrated or built-in appearance
* Butler’s pantry approximately 7’ x 18’
* Open dining area
* Large living/great room
* Strong connection between the kitchen, living room, dining area and covered back patio
* Mudroom/laundry approximately 14’ x 7’ connecting the garage to the house
* Large 3+ car side-entry garage
* Plenty of storage throughout the house

We would like to keep exterior doors intentional rather than having doors everywhere, while still having a beautiful connection to the backyard.

Kitchen & Entertaining

The kitchen is probably one of the most important spaces for us. We want it to feel grand and high-end, but we also actually cook and entertain, so functionality is extremely important.

We envision a large island, generous walkways, white-oak-style cabinetry, lots of storage, and a large window over the kitchen sink looking toward the backyard. We also want the butler’s pantry to function as an extension of the kitchen rather than feeling like a separate little room.

We want the kitchen, dining and living spaces to accommodate larger gatherings without the house feeling crowded.

Primary Suite

We want the primary suite to feel luxurious without dedicating an unnecessary amount of square footage to it.

For the bathroom, we like a spa-like feel with a large shower, freestanding tub, double vanity, wall-mounted faucets, sconces and an enclosed toilet room. We want the bathroom and closet arrangement to have a natural flow, but we do not want to have to walk through a wet/shower area to access the closet.

Privacy from the main living areas is also important to us.

Children’s Side of the House

We have three children, so their portion of the house needs to work well as they get older.

We would like our boys’ bedrooms to share a Jack-and-Jill bathroom with a shower, and we want our daughter’s bedroom/bathroom arrangement to have good privacy and storage.

Bedroom closets should be accessed from inside the bedrooms rather than through bathrooms whenever possible.

Garage, Laundry & Everyday Function

We would like a large side-entry garage with enough depth and width for larger vehicles, storage and normal everyday use.

The garage should lead into a mudroom/laundry area before entering the main house so there is a functional drop zone for shoes, backpacks, jackets, etc.

We want the “behind-the-scenes” spaces of the house—pantry, laundry, storage and garage—to be just as thoughtfully designed as the main rooms.

Property & Site

The home will be built on our approximately 10-acre property in the Sanger area of Fresno County. We already have a well on the property and have had the property surveyed.

Because we have a larger property, we would also like help making sure the orientation of the house makes sense for the site, including the driveway approach, front elevation, backyard/patio orientation, views, sun exposure and overall placement of the home.

Plans & Services We Need

We are looking for someone who can take our existing ideas/layout and help us turn them into a professional, buildable design.

Ideally, we would like to know whether you provide or coordinate everything necessary for a complete permit/construction plan set, including architectural plans, elevations, roof plan, foundation information, structural engineering, Title 24/energy documentation and any other plans or calculations required by Fresno County.

We are also interested in knowing how much involvement you have during the engineering/permitting process and whether revisions requested by the County are included in your services.

We would like to provide the floor plan we’ve been developing so you can see the direction we are already headed. We are absolutely open to changes—we don’t want someone to simply redraw what we’ve created. We want professional input on flow, proportions, functionality, structural practicality and opportunities to improve the design while keeping the major things that are important to us.

We are also very conscious of construction costs. Our overall goal is to create a beautiful custom home without designing something unnecessarily complicated or expensive to build. We would appreciate an architect who considers construction efficiency while designing.

Could you please let us know:

* What your design process looks like
* What is included in your services
* Whether you provide a complete permit-ready plan set
* What engineering/Title 24 work you handle or coordinate
* Your approximate fee structure for a project of this size
* How revisions are handled
* Your current timeline and availability
* Approximately how long it typically takes to go from initial design to permit-ready plans
* What information you would need from us to provide a proposal

We are excited to finally get this part of the project moving and are looking for someone who will work collaboratively with us to turn what we’ve been planning into a home that functions beautifully for our family.

Thank you,
Haley & Alvaro
